entries.name: Goblet Squat
entries.equipment: Dumbbell held at chest; clear stable floor
entries.purpose: Lower-body strength; squat pattern
entries.steps: Hold a dumbbell close to your chest. Set your feet at a comfortable width, bend your hips and knees to squat as far as you can control, then stand.
entries.cues: Keep the weight close; support your whole foot; let knees follow your toes.
entries.mistakes: Losing balance; dropping depth beyond control; letting the dumbbell drift away.
entries.easier: Bodyweight squat or supported sit-to-stand; shorten range.
entries.harder: Use a modest load increase or short controlled pause.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: Do not force depth or a particular stance. Use a load you can safely hold.

entries.name: Incline Push-Up
entries.equipment: Stable wall, counter or firmly anchored bench
entries.purpose: Upper-body pushing strength
entries.steps: Place hands on a stable raised surface. Step back to make a straight line from head to feet. Bend elbows to bring chest toward the support, then push away.
entries.cues: Use a surface that cannot slide or tip; control the trunk; allow shoulder blades to move.
entries.mistakes: Unsupported or unstable surface; hips dropping; elbows flaring excessively.
entries.easier: Use a higher support or wall.
entries.harder: Use a lower stable support; eventually floor push-up.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: The previous linked bent-knee push-up demonstration is not an exact incline push-up match; withheld pending demo verification.

entries.name: Standing Calf Raise
entries.equipment: Stable level surface; optional rail and external load
entries.purpose: Calf strength and ankle control
entries.steps: Stand tall with a comfortable straight-knee stance and stable support if needed. Rise onto the balls of your feet, pause briefly, lower under control.
entries.cues: Use a steady tempo and comfortable range; avoid rolling far to either side of the foot.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing to complete repetitions; unsupported balance loss; excessive ankle rolling.
entries.easier: Hold support and use both legs at modest range.
entries.harder: Progress to single leg or add a light manageable load.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: Start on level ground. A step is a separate range-of-motion progression.

entries.name: Dead Bug
entries.equipment: Mat or firm comfortable floor space
entries.purpose: Trunk control while arms and legs move
entries.steps: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent. Slowly reach one arm and the opposite leg away only as far as your trunk remains controlled, then return and alternate.
entries.cues: Exhale comfortably; keep your trunk position steady; shorten the reach when control changes.
entries.mistakes: Reaching so far the back arches sharply; holding the breath; rushing.
entries.easier: Move one limb at a time or perform small bent-knee heel taps.
entries.harder: Slow the reach or pause briefly at a manageable length.
entries.units: reps per side, sets
entries.safety: Do not forcefully flatten the lower back or extend further than you can control.

entries.name: Pallof Press
entries.equipment: Cable at chest height or securely anchored band
entries.purpose: Resist trunk rotation under light-to-moderate resistance
entries.steps: Stand side-on to a chest-height cable or approved band anchor, hold the handle close to your sternum, press away, pause, and return while maintaining a steady trunk.
entries.cues: Use manageable resistance; breathe; keep knees soft and a stable stance.
entries.mistakes: Allowing trunk to turn toward the anchor; using a questionable band anchor.
entries.easier: Reduce resistance or press through a shorter range.
entries.harder: Add a brief hold or small resistance increase.
entries.units: reps per side, hold seconds, sets
entries.safety: Use manufacturer-approved anchors; check clear pull path and stable footing.

entries.name: Suitcase Carry
entries.equipment: One dumbbell or kettlebell; clear walking area
entries.purpose: Loaded walking and lateral trunk control
entries.steps: Hold one weight at your side and walk with comfortable, controlled steps. Set the weight down safely and repeat on the other side as prescribed.
entries.cues: Stay naturally upright without leaning away from the weight; breathe continuously.
entries.mistakes: Excessive torso tilt; gripping too heavy a weight; walking into obstacles.
entries.easier: Lighter load, shorter distance or carry in smaller intervals.
entries.harder: Longer controlled time/distance or modestly heavier load.
entries.units: seconds per side, meters per side, sets
entries.safety: Suitcase March is related but a separate in-place exercise, not an exact alias.

entries.name: Adductor Rock-Back
entries.equipment: Mat; hands and knees with one leg extended to side
entries.readiness: Beginner if quadruped position is comfortable
entries.purpose: Controlled inner-thigh motion and tolerance
entries.steps: On hands and knees, extend one leg to the side with its foot supported. Slowly shift hips backward to a comfortable position, then forward again.
entries.cues: Keep movement easy and controlled; stop before pinching or sharp symptoms; avoid forcing range.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing into pain, aggressive twisting or forced end range.
entries.easier: Bring the leg closer; make the rock smaller.
entries.harder: Very gradually increase comfortable reach without forcing depth.
entries.units: reps per side
entries.safety: Avoid painful groin or pubic-area provocation; use individualized guidance for ongoing symptoms.

entries.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
entries.purpose: Upper-body horizontal pressing
entries.steps: Lie comfortably on your back with knees bent and dumbbells controlled above chest. Lower until upper arms gently meet the floor, then press upward.
entries.cues: Keep wrists stacked; control descent; do not bounce the arms on the floor.
entries.mistakes: Uncontrolled setup with heavy dumbbells; bouncing; forcing shoulder range.
entries.easier: Lighter dumbbells; separate incline push-up alternative.
entries.harder: Pause lightly near floor or progress load gradually.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: Ensure safe getting-into-position and getting-out-of-position with weights; no forced elbow flare.

entries.name: Pike Push-Up
entries.equipment: Hands and feet on stable non-slip surface
entries.purpose: Bodyweight shoulder-dominant pressing
entries.steps: From hands and feet, lift hips to form an inverted V. Bend elbows to lower head toward a point slightly ahead of the hands within a manageable range, then push up.
entries.cues: Keep hips high and use only a range you can control; breathe throughout.
entries.mistakes: Turning into a conventional push-up; losing hand traction; forcing head or neck position.
entries.easier: Shorter range or reduced incline; a lighter dumbbell press is a separate easier alternative.
entries.harder: More challenging angle or foot elevation when control is established.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: Not an entry-level first-day movement for everyone. Avoid rushed or head-first descents.

entries.name: Bird Dog
aliases: Quadruped Opposite Arm and Leg Reach
entries.readiness: Beginner if floor and wrist support are comfortable
entries.purpose: Trunk control with opposite-limb movement
entries.steps: Place hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Reach one leg back and opposite arm forward as far as you can hold stable, then return and switch sides.
entries.cues: Keep hips reasonably level; breathe; prioritize controlled reach over limb height.
entries.mistakes: Twisting or arching to lift higher; holding breath.
entries.easier: Extend only an arm or a leg, or use quadruped weight shifts.
entries.harder: Pause briefly at a controlled reach.
entries.units: reps per side, hold seconds
entries.safety: Wrist or knee intolerance may require changing the entire exercise rather than forcing the floor setup.

entries.name: Biceps Curl
entries.equipment: Dumbbells; stable standing or seated stance
entries.purpose: Elbow-flexor strength
entries.steps: Hold dumbbells alongside the body, bend elbows to raise the weights, then lower slowly while keeping shoulders reasonably still.
entries.cues: Choose controllable weight, move smoothly, avoid swinging the trunk.
entries.mistakes: Using body momentum; excessive shoulder movement; rushing lowering.
entries.easier: Use lighter weights or curl one arm at a time.
entries.harder: Add a brief top pause or slightly more weight with control.
entries.units: reps, sets
entries.safety: Dumbbell and other implement variations can share the family but should note setup differences.

entries.name: 90/90 Hip Lift-Off
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Sit in a supported 90/90 hip position. Keeping the thigh and pelvis as steady as practical, gently lift one ankle or knee a small distance, lower, and repeat before changing sides.
entries.cues: Use only the motion you can control without leaning, twisting or sharp discomfort.
entries.mistakes: Forcing a large range with momentum.
entries.easier: Lean back and use a very small lift.
entries.harder: Sit taller or hold the lift longer.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Sit with both knees bent at 90 degrees, one leg in front and one to the side, then rotate to switch which leg is in front.
entries.cues: Keep your chest tall and move slowly through the switch instead of using momentum.
entries.mistakes: Rushing the switch and losing control of the hips.
entries.easier: Use your hands on the floor for support during the switch.
entries.harder: Keep your hands off the floor entirely.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: A-Skip
entries.purpose: Build short-distance speed and the ability to produce force quickly.
entries.steps: Skip forward with a small hop on one foot while lifting the opposite knee; alternate legs with the opposite arm moving forward.
entries.cues: Use a comfortable rhythm and small travel distance; an A-march is an easier coordination option.
entries.mistakes: Rushing the skip or leaning back to lift the knee higher.
entries.easier: Switch to an A-march, moving slowly with deliberate opposite-arm timing.
entries.harder: Use a slightly quicker but still coordinated skip over a short distance.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: High Knees
entries.purpose: Build short-distance speed and the ability to produce force quickly.
entries.steps: A skipping drill driving one knee up high while the opposite arm drives forward, alternating quickly.
entries.cues: Focus on a quick, punchy knee drive rather than height alone.
entries.mistakes: Leaning back, stomping, or confusing speed with uncontrolled knee height.
entries.easier: March in place with alternating knee lifts and relaxed arm swings.
entries.harder: Increase cadence for a short, controlled burst without sacrificing posture.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Ankle Circles and Rocks
entries.purpose: Improve usable ankle motion for squatting, landing, and walking.
entries.steps: Circle each ankle slowly in both directions, then rock your weight forward and back over the ankle.
entries.cues: Keep the movement slow enough to feel every part of the range.
entries.mistakes: Rushing through without controlling the smaller ranges.
entries.easier: Reduce the size of the circle or rock.
entries.harder: Increase the range gradually.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Arm Circles
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Improve usable shoulder and shoulder-blade motion.
entries.steps: Stand comfortably and circle your arms through a small comfortable range, gradually changing size; reverse direction.
entries.cues: Keep your trunk relaxed and avoid forcing the shoulder range.
entries.mistakes: Forcing large painful circles or lifting the shoulders toward the ears.
entries.easier: Make smaller slow circles within a comfortable shoulder range.
entries.harder: Increase the comfortable arc or perform controlled circles in both directions.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Shoulder CAR
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Improve usable shoulder and shoulder-blade motion.
entries.steps: Stand with light support if needed. Slowly move one arm through a controlled shoulder circle while keeping the trunk steady; reverse and switch sides.
entries.cues: Use a smaller range when you cannot isolate the shoulder; do not force a full circle.
entries.mistakes: Twisting the trunk to imitate shoulder range or pushing through a painful pinch.
entries.easier: Trace a smaller slow arc with elbow softly bent and trunk quiet.
entries.harder: Increase the pain-free arc while keeping ribs and shoulders controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Machine-Assisted Pull-Up
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Use machine assistance to practice either a pull-up or dip pattern with controlled effort.
entries.steps: Set the machine counterweight and enter its platform according to the equipment instructions. Grip the pull-up handles, pull upward with control, then lower slowly.
entries.cues: More counterweight usually makes the exercise easier; confirm on the machine. Keep clear of moving parts.
entries.mistakes: Swinging the legs or dropping from the top without controlling the return.
entries.easier: Select more machine assistance and use a smooth range you can manage.
entries.harder: Reduce machine assistance slightly while maintaining a controlled descent.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Machine-Assisted Dip
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Use machine assistance to practice either a pull-up or dip pattern with controlled effort.
entries.steps: Set the counterweight, step or kneel onto the assisted platform as instructed, and hold the dip handles. Bend elbows to lower to a comfortable depth, then press up.
entries.cues: Use enough assistance to control the descent; do not force shoulder depth.
entries.mistakes: Dropping too deep at the shoulders or rushing the bottom position.
entries.easier: Use more machine assistance and a shoulder-comfortable dip depth.
entries.harder: Reduce assistance modestly without forcing a deeper shoulder position.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Barbell Back Squat
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Set the bar securely across your upper back in a suitable rack with safeties. Stand with feet at a comfortable width, brace your trunk, bend at the hips and knees to lower under control, then stand by pushing through the floor. Use lighter preparation sets before working sets.
entries.cues: Keep balanced pressure across the foot, a steady trunk and a squat depth you can control. Rest fully between challenging sets.
entries.mistakes: Losing balance, heels rising unintentionally or letting the trunk position collapse to reach depth.
entries.easier: Start with an unloaded squat or goblet squat; use a comfortable box target, a lighter bar or support as needed.
entries.harder: Add weight in small increments once all reps feel controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Hold a barbell, soften the knees and hinge to a stable torso position. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs, then lower under control.
entries.cues: Keep the trunk steady and use a load you can control without jerking.
entries.mistakes: Rounding the back, jerking the bar, or repeatedly standing taller to move the weight.
entries.easier: Use a lighter bar and a shallower hip hinge; practice the supported dumbbell row if needed.
entries.harder: Add a small amount of load while keeping the same trunk angle and control.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, soften the knees and hinge forward. Row the weights toward your ribs, then lower under control.
entries.cues: Keep the trunk steady; use a supported row if holding the hinge is difficult.
entries.mistakes: Shrugging the weight or twisting the trunk to finish each pull.
entries.easier: Reduce the weight and place one hand on a sturdy support if balance is difficult.
entries.harder: Increase weight gradually only if the torso stays still and the elbow path is controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Bear Crawl
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: Hands and feet on the floor, knees hovering just above it, crawl forward and back.
entries.cues: Keep your back flat and hips level. Imagine balancing a cup of water on your lower back.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips rise up higher than the shoulders.
entries.easier: Crawl in place without traveling.
entries.harder: Increase the distance or pace.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Barbell Bench Press
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the chest, shoulders, and triceps through a forward pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Lie on a stable bench with feet supported and eyes positioned near the bar. With safeties or a competent spotter, unrack, lower the bar toward the chest through a comfortable range, then press up and rerack.
entries.cues: Use a secure grip and controllable load; set rack safeties before lifting.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest, flaring elbows excessively, or lifting without safeties or a spotter when needed.
entries.easier: Use a lighter load in a properly set-up rack with safeties; a dumbbell or floor-press variation may be easier to manage.
entries.harder: Increase load modestly while preserving a smooth bar path and safe setup.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the chest, shoulders, and triceps through a forward pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Lie on a stable bench with feet supported and dumbbells controlled beside the chest. Press upward, then lower through a comfortable range.
entries.cues: Keep wrists stacked over forearms; plan a controlled way to get weights into and out of position.
entries.mistakes: Letting the wrists collapse or lowering the dumbbells beyond controlled shoulder range.
entries.easier: Choose lighter dumbbells or a dumbbell floor press for a more limited shoulder range.
entries.harder: Increase the load modestly while keeping wrists stacked and repetitions steady.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, raise light dumbbells out to the sides until level with your shoulders.
entries.cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands, and keep a slight bend in them.
entries.mistakes: Swinging the torso, shrugging, or turning the raise into a heavy row.
entries.easier: Use very light dumbbells and a smaller controlled arc.
entries.harder: Add small amounts of load or repetitions without losing shoulder control.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Bodyweight Hip Hinge
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hips, hamstrings, and back through a hip-hinge pattern.
entries.steps: With softly bent knees, push hips backward and tip the torso forward, then stand.
entries.cues: Practice a controlled hip hinge rather than reaching downward.
entries.mistakes: Rounding the lower back instead of hinging from the hips.
entries.easier: Easier: shorter movement. Progression equipment: dumbbell RDL.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo, or add a light weight across the shoulders.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Bodyweight Squat
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Sit hips back and down like reaching for a chair.
entries.cues: Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes, not caving in.
entries.mistakes: Lifting heels, collapsing inward, or forcing depth by rounding the trunk.
entries.easier: Hold a stable support or sit down onto a sturdy chair and stand; shorten the depth as needed.
entries.harder: Gradually squat a little deeper or add repetitions before considering a goblet squat.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat Jump
entries.purpose: Build power while practicing controlled takeoffs and landings.
entries.steps: Squat to a comfortable depth, then jump straight up. Land soft with bent knees.
entries.cues: Land with controlled hip and knee bend, settle your balance, and reset before the next repetition.
entries.mistakes: Landing with straight, locked knees.
entries.easier: Reduce jump height, or step up onto a low box instead.
entries.harder: Add a slight pause in the squat before jumping.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Standing Broad Jump
entries.purpose: Build power while practicing controlled takeoffs and landings.
entries.steps: Stand with enough clear landing space. Swing the arms and dip comfortably, jump forward, then land with both feet and absorb the landing through hips, knees and ankles. Hold a balanced landing before resetting for the next rep.
entries.cues: Prioritize a quiet, controlled landing and repeatable starting position; measure from the same takeoff line when testing.
entries.mistakes: Landing stiff-legged instead of absorbing through the knees and hips.
entries.easier: Make a shorter jump or use a small two-foot jump-and-stick (BFIT-00165) to rehearse landing control.
entries.harder: Chain jumps together with minimal reset time.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Burpees
entries.purpose: Build work capacity and the ability to repeat effort.
entries.steps: Squat down, kick feet back to a plank, optional push-up, jump feet back in, then jump up.
entries.cues: Move at a pace where your form holds up for the whole set, not just the first few reps.
entries.mistakes: Letting the lower back sag in the plank portion as fatigue builds.
entries.easier: Remove the push-up and the jump, stepping instead.
entries.harder: Add the push-up and a higher jump.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Cable Rotation
entries.equipment: Adjustable cable machine and suitable handle
entries.purpose: Build controlled trunk rotation and coordination through the hips and torso.
entries.steps: Standing sideways to the cable, rotate your torso to pull the handle across your body.
entries.cues: Rotate through your torso and hips together, not just your arms.
entries.mistakes: Twisting the low back abruptly or letting the cable pull the body off balance.
entries.easier: Reduce cable resistance and rotate through a smaller comfortable arc with feet planted.
entries.harder: Use a modest load increase or a slightly larger controlled rotation.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Cable Triceps Pressdown
entries.equipment: Adjustable cable machine and suitable handle
entries.purpose: Add focused training volume for the arms.
entries.steps: Elbows pinned at your sides, push the bar or rope down until arms are straight.
entries.cues: Keep your elbows locked in place. Only your forearms should move.
entries.mistakes: Swinging the shoulders or using body weight to force the handle downward.
entries.easier: Lower the stack weight and keep elbows comfortably near your sides.
entries.harder: Increase the load slightly after controlling both the pressdown and return.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Build calf strength and ankle control for walking, running, and jumping.
entries.steps: Adjust the standing calf machine and supports as directed. Keep knees comfortably straight, raise the heels, then lower through a controlled range.
entries.cues: Start with modest range and load; do not force the heels below the platform.
entries.mistakes: Using the machine to bounce the weight or allowing the heels to drop abruptly.
entries.easier: Use a lighter setting and a smaller controlled ankle range.
entries.harder: Add a modest load or a pause at the top while controlling the lowering phase.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Cat-Cow Flow
entries.purpose: Improve upper-back motion for reaching, rotation, and posture changes.
entries.steps: On hands and knees, alternate arching your back up (cat) and dropping your belly down (cow).
entries.cues: Lead each direction with your breath. Exhale into cat, inhale into cow.
entries.mistakes: Rushing through without linking the breath to the movement.
entries.easier: Reduce the range of the arch and dip.
entries.harder: Move more slowly, holding each end briefly.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Chest Press Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Strengthen the chest, shoulders, and triceps through a forward pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Adjust the seat so handles line up with mid-chest height, then press forward to extension.
entries.cues: Keep your back flat against the pad. Don't arch to move more weight.
entries.mistakes: Locking the elbows aggressively at the top.
entries.easier: Reduce the resistance.
entries.harder: Increase resistance once all reps feel controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Child’s Pose with Reach-Through
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Kneeling, hips back toward your heels, thread one arm underneath your body and rotate to look up, then switch.
entries.cues: Let the rotation come from your upper back, not by forcing your shoulder down.
entries.mistakes: Forcing the shoulder down instead of rotating naturally.
entries.easier: Reduce how far you reach through.
entries.harder: Pause briefly at the top of the rotation.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Chin-Up
entries.purpose: Use an underhand grip to train the lats and upper back while placing greater emphasis on the biceps than a pronated pull-up.
entries.steps: Hang from the bar with your palms facing you and hands around shoulder-width apart. Begin from a controlled hang, pull your elbows down, and raise your upper chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
entries.cues: Keep the ribs controlled, squeeze the bar, and think about pulling your elbows toward your sides rather than curling only with your arms.
entries.mistakes: Swinging, shortening the bottom position, or letting the shoulders roll forward while trying to force the chin over the bar.
entries.easier: Use an assisted pull-up machine, a resistance band, or controlled eccentric chin-ups.
entries.harder: Add a pause at the top or add external weight after you can complete every repetition through a controlled full range.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Clamshell
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent and feet together. Keep the pelvis stacked, open the top knee, then lower slowly.
entries.cues: Stop before the pelvis rolls backward.
entries.mistakes: Rolling the entire pelvis backward.
entries.easier: Use no band and a smaller range.
entries.harder: Add a light band or pause at the top.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Copenhagen Plank
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: Side plank position with the top leg resting on a bench, bottom leg lifted to meet it.
entries.cues: Keep your hips lifted and stacked. Don't let them sag toward the floor.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips drop as fatigue builds.
entries.easier: Rest the bottom knee on the floor for support.
entries.harder: Extend the hold time.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Curl to Press
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Combine an arm curl with an overhead press for upper-body strength and conditioning.
entries.steps: Curl the dumbbells to your shoulders, rotate your palms forward, then press overhead.
entries.cues: Keep the movement smooth and connected. Curl, rotate, press.
entries.mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight into the press.
entries.easier: Split the curl and press into two separate movements.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo throughout.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable

entries.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the glutes and improve force production through the hips.
entries.steps: Upper back on a bench, feet flat, a dumbbell resting on your hips, drive up to full hip extension.
entries.cues: Tuck your chin slightly and drive through your heels, not your toes.
entries.mistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top.
entries.easier: Remove the weight and use bodyweight only.
entries.harder: Add weight, or a pause at the top.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides. Step one foot backward, bend both knees into a controlled split position, then push through the front foot to return. Alternate sides as prescribed.
entries.cues: Keep a comfortable stance width, steady trunk and front-foot balance. Choose a depth that permits control rather than forcing both knees to 90 degrees.
entries.mistakes: Leaning the torso too far forward.
entries.easier: Begin with bodyweight, hold a stable support or reduce the depth and step length.
entries.harder: Add a pause at the bottom.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Supported One-Arm Dumbbell Row
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Support one hand on a stable bench or surface, hinge forward, and row the other dumbbell toward your ribs. Without a suitable surface, use a staggered stance with the free hand supported on the forward thigh and a lighter load.
entries.cues: Keep the torso controlled and avoid twisting to lift the weight.
entries.mistakes: Twisting the torso to help lift the weight.
entries.easier: Easier: lighter load. Alternatives: cable row or chest-supported row.
entries.harder: Add a pause at the top of each row.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the shoulders and triceps through an overhead pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Sit on a stable bench with back support if available, or stand with a stable stance and lighter load if needed. Start dumbbells around shoulder height and press upward through a comfortable path.
entries.cues: Keep wrists supported over forearms; avoid creating extra range by strongly arching the back. Let shoulder blades move upward.
entries.mistakes: Leaning back to press or allowing the ribs to flare as the weights move overhead.
entries.easier: Choose lighter dumbbells, a neutral grip, or press one arm at a time within a comfortable range.
entries.harder: Add small load increments while keeping the trunk steady and path controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hips, hamstrings, and back through a hip-hinge pattern.
entries.steps: Set a barbell at an appropriate starting height over the midfoot. Hinge and bend the knees to grip outside the legs, brace, push through the floor to stand, then return the bar under control.
entries.cues: Keep the bar close and avoid jerking it from the floor. Raise the starting height if needed.
entries.mistakes: Rounding or jerking the bar away from the floor, or losing balance over the feet.
entries.easier: Practice an unloaded hinge or start with the bar elevated on secure blocks and a light load.
entries.harder: Progress the load or range only when the bar stays close and trunk position remains controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
entries.equipment: Trap bar and appropriate plates; clear level floor
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hips, hamstrings, and back through a hip-hinge pattern.
entries.steps: Stand centered inside the trap bar with feet stable. Bend at the hips and knees to reach the handles, brace, push through the floor to stand tall, then lower the bar with control. Practice with a manageable load and a few gradual warm-up sets.
entries.cues: Use high handles or an elevated start when needed; maintain a balanced position inside the frame.
entries.mistakes: Pulling the trap bar with a sudden jerk or letting hips shoot up before the chest.
entries.easier: Use high handles or an elevated start, reduce the load, or first practice a bodyweight hip hinge.
entries.harder: Progress the load gradually; maintain a controlled start and finish every repetition.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Deep Squat Rock
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Settle into the bottom of a squat, holding on to something if needed, and gently rock side to side.
entries.cues: Keep your heels down if possible, and breathe steadily through the hold.
entries.mistakes: Letting the heels lift instead of finding a supported depth.
entries.easier: Hold onto a support, or don't go as deep.
entries.harder: Remove the support, or extend the hold time.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Easy Walk Reset
entries.purpose: Walk at an easy pace while letting your breathing, shoulders, and effort level settle.
entries.steps: Walk for 2-5 minutes at a relaxed pace. Let the arms swing naturally and allow your breathing to return toward normal.
entries.cues: Use a pace that feels restorative, not like another conditioning interval.
entries.mistakes: Walking so quickly that breathing stays elevated or turning the reset into extra training.
entries.easier: Walk for 60-90 seconds or march gently in place while holding support.
entries.harder: Add one or two minutes while keeping the same easy effort rather than increasing speed.
entries.units: minutes, distance, work/rest intervals
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Elbow and Forearm CARs
entries.purpose: Build tolerance and control in the hands, wrists, and forearms.
entries.steps: Rotate your forearm slowly from palm-up to palm-down while keeping your elbow tucked at your side.
entries.cues: Keep the elbow still. The rotation should come from the forearm, not the shoulder.
entries.mistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the body to fake more range.
entries.easier: Reduce the range of rotation.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo further.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Farmer Carry
entries.equipment: Two manageable weights; clear level space
entries.purpose: Build grip, trunk control, and whole-body strength while moving.
entries.steps: Hold one manageable weight in each hand and walk along a clear path with controlled steps. Set both weights down safely.
entries.cues: Stay naturally tall and breathe. A one-weight carry is the separate Suitcase Carry.
entries.mistakes: Leaning forward, rounding the back, or allowing the dumbbells to swing into the legs.
entries.easier: Carry lighter weights for a shorter clear walking distance.
entries.harder: Build walking distance first, then increase load while maintaining upright posture.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Fast Feet
entries.purpose: Build work capacity and the ability to repeat effort.
entries.steps: Quick, small in-and-out foot taps or steps, staying light and low.
entries.cues: Keep the steps quick and small rather than large and heavy.
entries.mistakes: Taking steps too big to stay quick.
entries.easier: Slow the tempo.
entries.harder: Increase the tempo.
entries.units: seconds, sets
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Fire Hydrant
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Start on hands and knees. Keep one knee bent, lift it gently to the side, then lower and switch sides as prescribed.
entries.cues: Keep the trunk and pelvis steady rather than rotating to lift higher.
entries.mistakes: Twisting the trunk or shifting all the weight away.
entries.easier: Use a smaller range.
entries.harder: Add a light band while maintaining control.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Floor or Seated Breathing Reset
entries.purpose: Sit or lie in a supported position and use slow, quiet breathing to help your body downshift.
entries.steps: Sit or lie comfortably with your body supported. Take 5-8 slow breaths, usually about 45-90 seconds. Breathe in gently through the nose and let the exhale stay relaxed and slightly longer.
entries.cues: Keep the jaw, neck, and shoulders relaxed. The breaths should feel quiet and comfortable rather than forced.
entries.mistakes: Trying to take the biggest possible breath, holding the breath, or continuing if you feel dizzy or lightheaded.
entries.easier: Take 3-5 normal, relaxed breaths in a comfortable seated position.
entries.harder: Continue for 8-10 breaths or make the exhale slightly longer without straining or adding long breath holds.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Foam Roller Reset
entries.purpose: Use manageable pressure for 30-45 seconds per rolling area, or 5-8 slow breaths in a supported chest-opening position.
entries.steps: Place the roller under the chosen muscle area and support your body with the floor or your hands. Roll for 30-45 seconds per area. When lying lengthwise for a chest-opening position, stay for 5-8 slow breaths (about 45-90 seconds).
entries.cues: Use light-to-moderate pressure and breathe normally. Follow rolling with easy movement instead of staying on one area for several minutes.
entries.mistakes: Rolling directly over a painful joint, numbness, or using extreme pressure.
entries.easier: Use less body weight on the roller or a softer roller.
entries.harder: Slow the roll and pause briefly on a comfortable area.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Full-Body Integration Flow
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Slowly link two or three joints together in one flowing movement. For example, a shoulder circle blending into a hip rotation.
entries.cues: Move slowly enough that you could stop and hold at any point in the flow.
entries.mistakes: Rushing through the flow instead of treating it as practice.
entries.easier: Link just two joints together instead of three.
entries.harder: Add a third joint, or slow the tempo further.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Glute Bridge
entries.purpose: Strengthen the glutes and improve force production through the hips.
entries.steps: Lying on your back, knees bent, feet flat, drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line.
entries.cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top rather than arching your lower back to get height.
entries.mistakes: Arching the lower back to push the hips higher or pushing through the toes only.
entries.easier: Lift the hips a shorter distance, keep ribs down, and pause when glutes engage.
entries.harder: Add a pause or repetitions, then progress to bridge marching after both hips stay level.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Glute Bridge Marching
entries.purpose: Strengthen the glutes and improve force production through the hips.
entries.steps: Hold a bridge position at the top, then alternate lifting one knee toward your chest at a time.
entries.cues: Keep your hips level and still while the working leg lifts. That's the whole point of the drill.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips drop every time a foot lifts.
entries.easier: March more slowly, or keep the lift height low.
entries.harder: Pause briefly with the knee lifted each rep.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Sliding Leg Curl
entries.equipment: Sliders or towels on a suitable smooth floor; mat
entries.purpose: Build hamstring strength through controlled knee flexion and eccentric lowering.
entries.steps: Lie on your back with heels on sliders or towels on a suitable smooth surface. Lift the hips to a manageable bridge, slide the heels away, then bend the knees to draw them back.
entries.cues: Use a short range first; keep control of the hips and heels.
entries.mistakes: Dropping hips or letting the sliding legs extend faster than you can control.
entries.easier: Slide one heel at a time or shorten the slide while keeping hips supported.
entries.harder: Work toward longer two-leg slides, then a controlled full curl.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
entries.equipment: Knee padding; secure ankle restraint and suitable assistance
entries.purpose: Build hamstring strength through controlled knee flexion and eccentric lowering.
entries.steps: Kneel on padding with ankles secured by equipment or an appropriate partner setup. Keep hips and trunk aligned, lean forward slowly from the knees, and use the hands or assistance to catch and return.
entries.cues: Begin with substantial assistance and a short range. Never use an uncertain ankle anchor.
entries.mistakes: Dropping suddenly from the knees or bending excessively at the hips.
entries.easier: Use assistance from a band or hands to catch and support the lowering phase; shorten the range.
entries.harder: Reduce assistance gradually while controlling more of the lowering movement.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Hand Open-and-Close
entries.purpose: Slowly spread the fingers, then close the hand into a relaxed fist to move the fingers without adding heavy grip tension.
entries.steps: Open the hand and spread the fingers through a comfortable range, then close into a relaxed fist. Repeat for 5-10 controlled repetitions per hand.
entries.cues: Move smoothly and keep the grip relaxed. The goal is motion, not squeezing as hard as possible.
entries.mistakes: Clenching the fist aggressively, forcing the fingers apart, or continuing through tingling or sharp pain.
entries.easier: Use a smaller range and perform fewer repetitions.
entries.harder: Pause for one or two seconds in the open and closed positions without increasing grip force.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Hanging Knee Raise
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: Hanging from a bar, raise your knees toward your chest without swinging.
entries.cues: Curl your pelvis slightly at the top instead of just swinging your legs up.
entries.mistakes: Using momentum and swinging instead of a controlled lift.
entries.easier: Bend the knees less, or use ab-strap support.
entries.harder: Straighten the legs for a longer lever.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Hip Abduction Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Strengthen the muscles that move the hips outward and inward using a controlled machine range.
entries.steps: Adjust the seat and pads according to the machine. Press the thighs outward against resistance, then return slowly.
entries.cues: Use a comfortable range without rocking the trunk or bouncing the stack.
entries.mistakes: Rocking the trunk or forcing the legs outward with momentum.
entries.easier: Lower the machine resistance and use a smaller pain-free motion.
entries.harder: Add a small amount of resistance while keeping the pelvis stable.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Hip Adduction Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Strengthen the muscles that move the hips outward and inward using a controlled machine range.
entries.steps: Adjust the seat and inner-thigh pads according to the machine. Bring the thighs inward against resistance, then return slowly.
entries.cues: Choose a modest starting width and controllable load; do not force a stretch.
entries.mistakes: Forcing the legs inward through groin pain or using momentum to move the stack.
entries.easier: Lower the resistance and stay in a comfortable range; skip if groin symptoms occur.
entries.harder: Increase the comfortable range or load gradually without groin discomfort.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Standing Hip CAR
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Hold stable support, lift one knee and slowly move the thigh through a small controlled circle, then reverse and switch sides.
entries.cues: Keep the pelvis mostly still; reduce the circle instead of twisting the trunk.
entries.mistakes: Tilting the trunk or hiking the hip to fake a larger hip circle.
entries.easier: Hold a support, reduce the circle size, and move slowly.
entries.harder: Make the controlled circle slightly larger while keeping pelvis steady.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Quadruped Hip CAR
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Start on hands and knees. Move one bent leg through a slow comfortable circle at the hip, reverse, then switch sides.
entries.cues: Keep the pelvis steady and avoid forcing the range.
entries.mistakes: Arching the low back or turning the pelvis while moving the lifted hip.
entries.easier: Use a smaller slow circle with both hands and supporting knee stable.
entries.harder: Increase the circle size only while the trunk stays still.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Inchworm
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: From standing, hinge forward, walk the hands out to a plank, then walk the feet or hands back in.
entries.cues: Move under control and keep the range comfortable for the hamstrings and back.
entries.mistakes: Rushing, dropping the hips, or forcing straight knees.
entries.easier: Bend the knees more or shorten the walkout.
entries.harder: Add a controlled push-up only when the basic version feels easy.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Two-Foot Jump Rope Bounce
entries.purpose: Build work capacity and the ability to repeat effort.
entries.steps: Use a suitable rope with clear floor and overhead space. Turn the rope with relaxed wrist movement and make small two-foot bounces as it passes under the feet.
entries.cues: Keep jumps low; practice without the rope if timing is difficult.
entries.mistakes: Jumping too high, which wastes energy and disrupts rhythm.
entries.easier: Easier: pogos without the rope if impact is suitable; step-pattern practice if it is not.
entries.harder: Increase pace, or add double-unders once basic timing is solid.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Seated Knee CAR
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Build controlled knee motion through a comfortable range.
entries.steps: Sit with the thigh supported and foot clear of the floor. Gently bend and straighten the knee; with it bent, make small controlled inward and outward lower-leg rotations.
entries.cues: Use small unloaded motion; do not twist a planted foot or force rotation.
entries.mistakes: Moving from the hip instead of isolating the knee.
entries.easier: Reduce the size of the circle.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo further.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Lat Pulldown
entries.purpose: Strengthen the back and arms through an overhead pulling pattern.
entries.steps: Adjust the seat and thigh pad securely. Take a comfortable grip on the pulldown bar, begin with arms extended overhead, draw elbows down to bring the bar toward the upper chest, then return slowly without letting the weight stack slam.
entries.cues: Maintain a mostly stable torso and shoulders moving comfortably; use the arms and upper back rather than swinging backward.
entries.mistakes: Using body momentum to yank the bar down.
entries.easier: Use less resistance or a securely anchored band pulldown (BFIT-00154) with controlled range.
entries.harder: Increase resistance, or slow the release phase.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Lateral Bound
entries.purpose: Build power while practicing controlled takeoffs and landings.
entries.steps: Push sideways from one foot and land on the opposite foot with the hip and knee comfortably bent. Hold the landing until balanced, then reset and travel back in the other direction.
entries.cues: Stick each landing before repeating; reduce travel distance when balance or alignment becomes inconsistent.
entries.mistakes: Landing with a stiff, straight leg.
entries.easier: Make a smaller bound, or begin with a controlled lateral step-and-stick before adding a jump.
entries.harder: Bound further, or chain reps together without a full stop.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Supported Lateral Lunge
entries.equipment: Bodyweight; stable rail or fixed support; optional dumbbell held only if appropriate
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Hold a stable support. Step sideways, bend the stepping knee and sit into that hip while the other leg stays relatively straight. Return under control.
entries.cues: Keep the working foot supported and knee aligned with its toes. Start shallow rather than forcing a deep stretch.
entries.mistakes: Letting the stepping knee cave inward or forcing an aggressive groin stretch.
entries.easier: Hold a sturdy support, take a shorter step and stay shallow.
entries.harder: Gradually increase the lateral step or depth without losing alignment.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Hold a manageable dumbbell at the chest. Step to one side, bend that knee and sit into that hip while the other leg stays relatively straight. Push back and repeat as prescribed.
entries.cues: Keep the working foot supported and use a comfortable step and depth.
entries.mistakes: Rushing sideways, tipping the torso excessively, or forcing depth under load.
entries.easier: Remove the dumbbell and perform a supported, shallow lateral lunge.
entries.harder: Add modest load or controlled depth once bodyweight form is steady.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Lateral Shuffle
entries.purpose: Practice changing direction with control and efficient foot placement.
entries.steps: Use a clear space. Move sideways with short steps, keeping feet from crossing, then slow before reversing.
entries.cues: Start at a controlled pace. This is not a maximal agility test.
entries.mistakes: Standing too tall, which slows your ability to change direction.
entries.easier: Easier: lateral step-touch.
entries.harder: Increase speed or add a direction-change cue.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Leg Extension
entries.purpose: Strengthen the quadriceps through controlled knee extension.
entries.steps: Shins behind the pad, extend your legs until nearly straight, then lower with control.
entries.cues: Control the lowering phase just as much as the lift.
entries.mistakes: Letting the weight drop quickly on the way down.
entries.easier: Reduce resistance or range.
entries.harder: Increase resistance, or add a pause at the top.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Leg Press
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Feet shoulder-width on the platform, lower until knees reach about 90 degrees, then press back out.
entries.cues: Don't let your lower back round off the pad at the bottom.
entries.mistakes: Locking the knees out hard at the top of every rep.
entries.easier: Reduce the range or the weight.
entries.harder: Increase weight once form is consistent.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Med Ball Rotational Throw
entries.purpose: Build rotational power and coordination through the trunk and hips.
entries.steps: Use an appropriate medicine ball and a safe throwing wall or clearly marked partner setup. Stand side-on with enough rebound space, rotate through hips and torso to throw across the body, then reset between efforts.
entries.cues: Generate power from coordinated hip and trunk rotation; keep the throw area clear and use a ball suitable for the wall or partner.
entries.mistakes: Using an unsuitable wall or hard-rebound ball, crowding the rebound zone, or throwing only with the arms.
entries.easier: Use a lighter ball, practice a slow unloaded torso turn, or use a controlled rotational chest pass in an approved space.
entries.harder: Use a heavier ball, or add a small step into the throw.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Mountain Climbers
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: In a high plank, drive your knees toward your chest one at a time in a running motion.
entries.cues: Keep your hips low and steady. Don't let them pike up as you speed up.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips rise as fatigue sets in.
entries.easier: Slow the pace significantly.
entries.harder: Increase the speed once form holds.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Gentle Neck Rotation
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Improve comfortable neck motion and control.
entries.steps: Sit or stand comfortably. Slowly turn your head to look right, return to center, then left.
entries.cues: Keep the movement easy and unforced. Turn side to side without circling your head.
entries.mistakes: Forcing the head into a painful end range or turning the shoulders with the head.

entries.harder: Slowly explore a slightly wider comfortable range, never forcing it.
