entries.name: Chin Tuck
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Improve comfortable neck motion and control.
entries.steps: Sit or stand comfortably and gently draw the chin straight backward, making a small double-chin motion, then release.
entries.cues: Keep the eyes level; do not force the head down or hold your breath.
entries.mistakes: Tilting the chin up or down instead of drawing it gently backward.
entries.easier: Make a small chin glide while sitting upright with the eyes level.
entries.harder: Hold the gentle retraction briefly without tensing the neck.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Gentle Neck Half-Circle
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Improve comfortable neck motion and control.
entries.steps: From a comfortable seated position, lower the chin slightly and make a small slow arc toward one shoulder, return through center, then toward the other.
entries.cues: Stay in a comfortable front half-circle; avoid forcing the head backward or moving through symptoms.
entries.mistakes: Dropping the head backward or making a large forced full neck circle.
entries.easier: Use small, slow side-to-side movements in the comfortable front half of the arc.
entries.harder: Slightly expand the comfortable half-circle while avoiding pressure or dizziness.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Barbell Overhead Press
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the shoulders and triceps through an overhead pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Start with the bar at upper-chest height in a stable stance. Brace, press overhead through a comfortable path, then lower with control.
entries.cues: Avoid leaning back to complete the lift; use appropriate rack height and manageable load.
entries.mistakes: Overarching the low back or pushing the bar away from the body to clear the head.
entries.easier: Use a lighter bar and controlled overhead range; a dumbbell press may suit some readers.
entries.harder: Increase load gradually while keeping balance and trunk control.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Squat
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Press one light dumbbell straight overhead, arm locked out, then squat while keeping it there.
entries.cues: Keep your eyes forward and the weight stacked directly over your shoulder, not drifting ahead.
entries.mistakes: Letting the arm drift forward as the squat gets harder.
entries.easier: Lower the weight to shoulder height instead of overhead.
entries.harder: Slow the descent to 3 seconds.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Pelvic Tilt
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Lie on your back with knees bent or stand against a wall, then gently alternate between flattening and releasing the low back.
entries.cues: Use a small motion and breathe normally.
entries.mistakes: Turning it into a large bridge or holding the breath.
entries.easier: Make the movement smaller.
entries.harder: Pause for two seconds at each end without bracing hard.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Forearm Plank
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: Forearms and toes on the floor, body in a straight line from head to heels.
entries.cues: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core like you're about to be poked in the stomach.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike up.
entries.easier: Drop to your knees, or shorten the hold time.
entries.harder: Extend the hold, or lift one foot briefly.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: From a high plank, tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, alternating sides.
entries.cues: Keep your hips as still as possible. The less they rock, the more it's working.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips rotate side to side with each tap.
entries.easier: Widen your feet for more stability.
entries.harder: Narrow your feet, or slow the tap.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Prone Y Raise
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Lie face-down with arms angled overhead in a Y. Reach long, lift the arms a small distance, then lower.
entries.cues: Keep the neck comfortable and avoid shrugging.
entries.mistakes: Arching the lower back to create height.
entries.easier: Slide the hands on the floor.
entries.harder: Lift the arms or add a brief hold.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Pulse Squat to Frog Squat
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Small pulsing squats in a narrow stance, then switch to a wide, toes-out frog squat pulse.
entries.cues: Keep the pulses small and controlled. This is about time under tension, not speed.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing instead of controlling the small range of motion.
entries.easier: Reduce the range of the pulse.
entries.harder: Add a 1-second pause at the bottom of each pulse.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Punches to Squat Combo
entries.purpose: Combine punches and squats for full-body conditioning and coordination.
entries.steps: Throw two light-dumbbell punches, then drop into one bodyweight squat. Repeat.
entries.cues: Keep your core braced through the punches so your torso doesn't twist wildly.
entries.mistakes: Rushing the punches and losing squat form.
entries.easier: Remove the dumbbell and punch with open hands.
entries.harder: Add a small hop out of the squat.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Plank Jack
entries.purpose: Build conditioning and trunk control while moving the feet in and out from a plank.
entries.steps: From a push-up plank position, hop both feet out wide, then hop them back together.
entries.cues: Keep your hips level and core braced through the hop. Don't let them bounce up and down.
entries.mistakes: Letting the lower back sag as fatigue sets in.
entries.easier: Step the feet out and in instead of hopping.
entries.harder: Add a push-up between each jack.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Push-Up
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Strengthen the chest, shoulders, and triceps through a forward pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Place hands slightly wider than shoulders on the floor and step the feet back. Keep the body controlled as you bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press away.
entries.cues: Use an incline if you cannot keep the trunk steady through the range.
entries.mistakes: Dropping the hips, flaring elbows excessively, or reaching the chin rather than lowering the body together.
entries.easier: Perform incline push-ups on a stable elevated surface.
entries.harder: Gradually lower the hand support height or add controlled reps.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
entries.equipment: Clear space; stable seat or support if specified
entries.purpose: Strengthen the chest, shoulders, and triceps through a forward pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Set up for a floor push-up with hands modestly wider than your usual position. Lower through a comfortable shoulder range, then press up.
entries.cues: A wider grip is a variation, not a requirement; do not force extreme hand width.
entries.mistakes: Placing hands so wide that shoulder position feels unstable or painful.
entries.easier: Move the hands closer to a regular push-up width or use a stable incline.
entries.harder: Add repetitions with a controlled range; wider hand placement is not required for progress.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Pull-Up
entries.purpose: Use a pronated grip to train the lats and upper back while the biceps assist the movement.
entries.steps: Hang from the bar with your palms facing away and hands around shoulder-width apart. Begin from a controlled hang, pull your elbows down and slightly back, and raise your upper chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
entries.cues: Keep the ribs controlled and imagine driving your elbows toward your hips so your back, not momentum, is the main driver.
entries.mistakes: Kicking or kipping, shrugging toward the ears, or cutting the repetition short at the bottom.
entries.easier: Use an assisted pull-up machine, a resistance band, or a lat pulldown while building the required strength.
entries.harder: Add a pause near the top or add external weight after you can complete controlled full-range repetitions.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Supported Hip Airplane
entries.equipment: Bodyweight; stable rail, rack or wall for hand support
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Stand on one leg in a small supported hip hinge, keeping one or both hands on a stable rail or wall. Rotate the pelvis open and then closed around the stance hip while the foot stays grounded. Return to a balanced position before repeating.
entries.cues: Move from the hip and pelvis rather than turning the shoulders alone; use as much hand support as needed.
entries.mistakes: Turning from the shoulders instead of the hip.
entries.easier: Use two hands on a wall, a smaller hinge angle and a reduced rotation range.
entries.harder: Use less support or add a light load.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Renegade Row
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: In a plank with hands on dumbbells, row one dumbbell up to your hip while balancing on the other arm.
entries.cues: Keep your hips square to the floor. Resist the urge to rotate as you row.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips rotate or sag during the row.
entries.easier: Widen your feet for more stability, or drop to your knees.
entries.harder: Narrow your foot stance to increase the balance challenge.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Repeat Sprint Intervals
entries.purpose: Build short-distance speed and the ability to produce force quickly.
entries.steps: Short, near-maximal sprints (e.g., 20 meters) with full recovery between efforts.
entries.cues: Prioritize quality. Each sprint should be close to your best effort, not a pace you can sustain forever.
entries.mistakes: Not resting long enough between sprints, turning it into a conditioning drill instead of a speed drill.
entries.easier: Shorten the sprint distance or extend the rest.
entries.harder: Add more repeats, or shorten the rest between them.
entries.units: minutes, distance, work/rest intervals
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Reverse Snow Angel
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Lying face down, sweep your arms from your sides up overhead and back, like making a snow angel.
entries.cues: Keep your chest and head gently lifted, squeezing your upper back throughout.
entries.mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears instead of squeezing the back.
entries.easier: Reduce the range of the arm sweep.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo, or hold light weights.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
entries.equipment: Dumbbell(s); stable bench or support when specified in the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hips, hamstrings, and back through a hip-hinge pattern.
entries.steps: Stand with your feet at a comfortable hip-width stance and hold the dumbbells near your thighs. Soften your knees, then send your hips backward while keeping the weights close to your legs. Stop before you need to round or strain to go lower. Push through your feet and bring your hips forward to stand tall.
entries.cues: Stop where you can maintain control; reaching the floor is unnecessary. Avoid turning the movement into a deep squat.
entries.mistakes: Rounding the lower back, squatting the movement, or lowering farther than hip mobility permits.
entries.easier: Practice a bodyweight hip hinge or use lighter dumbbells with a shorter lowering distance.
entries.harder: Increase load slightly while keeping the weights close and maintaining the hinge.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
entries.equipment: Barbell and appropriate plates; rack, bench and safeties when required by the setup
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hips, hamstrings, and back through a hip-hinge pattern.
entries.steps: Hold a barbell near the thighs with softly bent knees. Send the hips backward while keeping the bar close; stop at a controllable range, then stand.
entries.cues: Keep the movement at the hips; touching the floor is not required.
entries.mistakes: Letting the bar drift forward or rounding the back to reach a lower position.
entries.easier: Use an unloaded/light bar, shorten the lowering range, and practice a hip hinge.
entries.harder: Increase load gradually without losing a controlled hip hinge or bar proximity.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Russian Twists
entries.purpose: Build rotational power and coordination through the trunk and hips.
entries.steps: Seated with knees bent, lean back slightly and rotate your torso side to side.
entries.cues: Rotate from your ribcage, not just by swinging your arms.
entries.mistakes: Moving fast instead of controlling the rotation.
entries.easier: Keep your feet on the floor for more stability.
entries.harder: Lift your feet off the floor, or hold a light weight.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Scapular Circle
entries.purpose: Improve usable shoulder and shoulder-blade motion.
entries.steps: Keep the arms relaxed or place the hands on a wall, then move the shoulder blades up, back, down, and forward in a slow circle.
entries.cues: Let the shoulder blades glide without shrugging aggressively.
entries.mistakes: Bending the elbows or moving only the neck.
entries.easier: Use a smaller circle.
entries.harder: Use a wall-supported plank position for more control demand.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Seated Leg Curl
aliases: Leg curl: seated or lying machine
entries.purpose: Strengthen the hamstrings through controlled knee flexion.
entries.steps: Pad behind your ankles, curl your heels toward your seat, then release with control.
entries.cues: Keep your hips pressed into the seat throughout the movement.
entries.mistakes: Swinging the weight or lifting the hips off the seat to force the last repetitions.
entries.easier: Use a lighter stack setting and a smaller comfortable knee-bending arc.
entries.harder: Add a few repetitions or a modest load increase while returning slowly.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Seated Row Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Sit tall, chest against the pad if available, pull the handles to your torso.
entries.cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades at the end.
entries.mistakes: Leaning back excessively to move more weight.
entries.easier: Reduce resistance.
entries.harder: Increase resistance, or add a brief pause at full contraction.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Shadowboxing
entries.purpose: Build work capacity and the ability to repeat effort.
entries.steps: Stand with a comfortable staggered stance and throw relaxed alternating punches into the air, returning hands to a ready position.
entries.cues: Do not snap the elbows into hard lockout. Allow comfortable foot and hip movement.
entries.mistakes: Locking out the elbows aggressively on every punch.
entries.easier: Easier: slower punches with minimal stepping. No weights needed.
entries.harder: Increase pace or add head movement between punches.
entries.units: minutes, distance, work/rest intervals
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Shoulder Press Machine
entries.equipment: Named exercise machine adjusted according to its instructions
entries.purpose: Strengthen the shoulders and triceps through an overhead pressing pattern.
entries.steps: Adjust seat height so handles start at shoulder level, press up to full extension.
entries.cues: Keep your back flat against the pad through the whole set.
entries.mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
entries.easier: Reduce resistance.
entries.harder: Increase resistance once form is consistent.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
entries.purpose: Strengthen the glutes and improve force production through the hips.
entries.steps: Same setup as a glute bridge, but one foot lifted and extended as you drive the hips up.
entries.cues: Keep your hips level. Don't let the lifted-leg side dip down.
entries.mistakes: Rotating the hips to compensate for the lifted leg.
entries.easier: Keep both feet down and simply shift more weight to one side.
entries.harder: Add a pause at the top of each rep.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Stand on one leg, hinge forward while the other leg extends back for balance, like a tipping scale.
entries.cues: Keep your hips square to the floor. Don't let them rotate open.
entries.mistakes: Rushing the movement and losing balance.
entries.easier: Use a light touch-point for balance, or shorten the range.
entries.harder: Add a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Split Squat
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Take a staggered stance with feet comfortably apart and rear heel lifted. Lower vertically by bending both knees through a controlled range, then press through the front foot to stand. Complete both sides as prescribed.
entries.cues: Keep balance over the front foot, knee tracking comfortably with the toes and trunk steady. Choose a depth that remains controlled.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom, narrowing the stance until balance is lost or letting the front knee collapse inward.
entries.easier: Use bodyweight, hold a rack or rail for balance, or shorten the range before adding load.
entries.harder: Add dumbbells, or slow the descent.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat Thrust
entries.purpose: Build full-body conditioning by moving between standing, squat, and plank positions.
entries.steps: From standing, squat down, place hands on the floor, jump feet back to a plank, then jump them back in and stand.
entries.cues: Keep your core tight through the plank moment instead of letting your hips sag.
entries.mistakes: Letting the lower back arch during the plank position.
entries.easier: Step the feet back and in instead of jumping.
entries.harder: Add a small hop at the top.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat to Alternating Reverse Lunge
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Perform one bodyweight squat, then step one leg back into a reverse lunge. Alternate lunge sides each rep.
entries.cues: Keep your front knee tracking over your foot on the lunge portion.
entries.mistakes: Rushing the transition and losing balance on the lunge step.
entries.easier: Break the squat and lunge into two separate, slower movements.
entries.harder: Add a small hop between transitions.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat to Press
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Hold a dumbbell at shoulder height, squat down, then press it overhead as you stand.
entries.cues: Use the stand-up drive from your legs to help start the press.
entries.mistakes: Arching the lower back to finish the overhead press.
entries.easier: Separate the two movements. Squat, stand, then press.
entries.harder: Add a slight pause in the squat before standing.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat-to-Reach
entries.purpose: Build active control through a usable range of motion.
entries.steps: Sit into a comfortable squat, then stand or remain supported while reaching one or both arms overhead.
entries.cues: Keep the feet grounded and use a squat depth you can control.
entries.mistakes: Collapsing the knees inward or forcing depth.
entries.easier: Use a chair target or hold a stable support.
entries.harder: Reach farther or pause in the bottom position without losing balance.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Squat to Upright Row
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Hold a dumbbell with both hands in front of your thighs. Squat, then row the weight up to chest height as you stand.
entries.cues: Lead the row with your elbows, not your wrists.
entries.mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears during the row.
entries.easier: Do the squat and row as two separate, slower movements.
entries.harder: Add a brief pause at the top of the row.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Steady-State Cardio
entries.purpose: Build work capacity and the ability to repeat effort.
entries.steps: Pick a pace you can sustain for the full duration without stopping.
entries.cues: Aim for a pace where you could hold a broken conversation, not a sprint.
entries.mistakes: Starting too fast and burning out halfway through.
entries.easier: Reduce duration or intensity.
entries.harder: Increase duration, incline, or resistance.
entries.units: minutes, distance, work/rest intervals
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Step-Up
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Place one foot fully on a step or bench, drive through that heel to stand up on it.
entries.cues: Push through the working leg. Avoid pushing off the bottom foot to help.
entries.mistakes: Pushing off the bottom foot instead of driving through the top leg.
entries.easier: Use a lower step.
entries.harder: Use a higher step, or add a knee drive at the top (Step-Up to High Knee).
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Sumo Squat
entries.purpose: Strengthen the legs through a squat pattern.
entries.steps: Feet wide, toes turned out, one dumbbell held with both hands between your legs.
entries.cues: Keep your chest tall and drive your knees out in line with your toes.
entries.mistakes: Rounding forward instead of sitting straight down.
entries.easier: Narrow the stance slightly or use a lighter weight.
entries.harder: Add a pause at the bottom.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Superman
entries.purpose: Train the trunk to resist unwanted movement and transfer force.
entries.steps: Lying face down, simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs slightly off the floor.
entries.cues: Lift only a few inches. This is about control, not height.
entries.mistakes: Yanking upward instead of lifting with control.
entries.easier: Lift arms and legs separately instead of together.
entries.harder: Add a brief hold at the top.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Inverted Table Row
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Only use a structure confirmed suitable to support your bodyweight without tipping or sliding. Grip the edge from underneath with feet grounded, pull the chest toward it, then lower.
entries.cues: If the structure or grip is uncertain, use purpose-built row equipment or another pulling exercise.
entries.mistakes: Using an unstable table, allowing the hips to sag, or pulling suddenly on the support.
entries.easier: Do not use furniture unless it is purpose-built and verified secure; use a stable gym suspension trainer or supported dumbbell row instead.
entries.harder: Move feet slightly forward on a secure rated setup to increase the challenge while keeping the body straight.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Anchored Towel Row
entries.purpose: Strengthen the upper back and pulling muscles.
entries.steps: Use an undamaged towel and an anchor specifically suitable to support your bodyweight. Hold the ends, lean back with feet grounded, pull your torso toward the anchor, then lower.
entries.cues: Do not rely on an unverified door handle or household fixture; choose another row if the anchor cannot be confirmed.
entries.mistakes: Anchoring a towel to an unsecured door or handle, or leaning back farther than the anchor can support.
entries.easier: Use a purpose-built, load-rated anchor and stand more upright; otherwise substitute a supported dumbbell or cable row.
entries.harder: Step farther from a certified fixed anchor only after confirming it is secure and form is controlled.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Side-Lying Open Book
entries.purpose: Improve upper-back motion for reaching, rotation, and posture changes.
entries.steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent and arms reaching forward. Open the top arm and chest backward, then return.
entries.cues: Keep knees comfortably stacked and follow the hand with your eyes if comfortable. Your opening hand does not need to reach the floor.
entries.mistakes: Letting the hips rotate along with the chest instead of staying stacked.
entries.easier: Easier: a smaller turn with your head supported. Standing option: stand comfortably and gently turn your chest, letting your hips and feet turn with you. Return and repeat on the other side.
entries.harder: Pause briefly at the end range, or slow the tempo.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Toe Flexion and Extension
entries.purpose: Build control and comfortable motion through the toes and forefoot.
entries.steps: Seated or standing with support, lift and lower the toes or gently curl and spread them.
entries.cues: Move slowly and keep the heel supported.
entries.mistakes: Cramping from gripping too hard.
entries.easier: Use a seated position.
entries.harder: Perform one foot at a time or add a short hold.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Bench Dip
entries.purpose: Strengthen the triceps, chest, and shoulders through a dip pattern.
entries.steps: Hands on a bench behind you, lower your body by bending your elbows, then press back up.
entries.cues: Keep your elbows pointing backward, not flaring out to the sides.
entries.mistakes: Lowering too far, which can strain the shoulders.
entries.easier: Keep your knees bent and feet close to reduce the load.
entries.harder: Straighten your legs further out, or add weight.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Walking Hamstring Sweep
entries.purpose: Improve usable hip motion and control.
entries.steps: Step forward, hinge over the front leg with a flat back, sweeping your hands toward your foot, then step through.
entries.cues: Keep a flat back and only go as low as your hamstrings allow without rounding.
entries.mistakes: Rounding the back to reach further.
entries.easier: Reduce how far you hinge forward.
entries.harder: Slow the tempo and hold briefly at the bottom of each sweep.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Walking Lunge
entries.purpose: Build single-leg strength, balance, and hip control.
entries.steps: Step forward into a lunge, then bring the back foot through into the next step.
entries.cues: Keep your torso tall. Resist the urge to lean forward to catch your balance.
entries.mistakes: Taking too short a step, which pushes weight onto the front knee.
entries.easier: Do stationary lunges instead of walking ones.
entries.harder: Add dumbbells.
entries.units: repetitions, sets; per side where applicable
entries.safety: Use the setup and dosage specified in your guide. Stop if pain or loss of control changes the movement.

entries.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rock
entries.purpose: Build controlled ankle dorsiflexion through a usable range.

entries.name: Short-Lever Copenhagen Hold
entries.equipment: Stable sturdy bench or padded support; clear mat
entries.readiness: Intermediate; start with comfortable groin loading
entries.purpose: Sustained inner-thigh and lateral trunk loading with a short support lever
entries.steps: Lie side-on with the top knee supported on a stable bench and top hip extended. Support the torso on the lower forearm; lift the pelvis until the torso and top thigh form a controlled line. Keep the lower knee bent or lightly supported as needed; hold, then switch sides.
entries.cues: Bench supports the KNEE, not the ankle; keep pelvis stacked, breathe, and stop before losing hip position.
entries.mistakes: Resting on the ankle (changes to long lever); dropping the hips; forcing through groin pain.
entries.easier: Keep the lower leg on the floor for assistance; shorten hold or use a lower, stable support.
entries.harder: Lengthen hold gradually or progress to the distinct long-lever version when prepared.
entries.units: seconds per side, sets
entries.safety: Avoid sharp groin or pubic pain. Do not substitute the legacy generic Copenhagen entry as an exact how-to.

entries.name: Single-Leg Straight-Knee Calf Isometric Hold
entries.equipment: Stable level floor; rail or sturdy support; optional appropriate load

entries.purpose: Sustained plantarflexor force and balance control with a relatively straight knee
entries.steps: Stand tall beside stable support. Rise onto the ball of one foot, keeping the working knee softly straight, then hold the heel raised at a controlled height without bouncing. Lower slowly and repeat on the other side.
entries.cues: Use hand support to remove balance as a limitation; do not lock knee aggressively; hold a stable heel height.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing, rolling the ankle, letting heel sink with fatigue, or gripping support unsafely.
entries.easier: Use a supported two-leg heel-raised hold on level ground.
entries.harder: Increase hold duration or carefully add external load when tolerated.
entries.units: seconds per leg, sets
entries.safety: Sustained loading is not a guarantee of tendon injury prevention; stop for new or escalating tendon pain.

entries.cues: Keep knees comfortably bent; hold near a controllable mid-to-high heel-rise and breathe normally.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing through the hold, unsafe pad adjustment, losing contact with foot platform.

entries.harder: Increase load modestly before maximizing hold duration if position stays steady.
entries.units: seconds per leg or both legs, sets
entries.safety: Use equipment instructions. If unilateral machine setup is unsafe, perform both legs and record the change.

entries.steps: Stand with most weight through the front foot and the opposite foot slightly behind on the toes as a kickstand. Keep hips mostly square, bend the front knee slightly, hinge backward through the front hip, then return to standing.
entries.cues: Rear foot is a BALANCE kickstand, not a second equal loading leg; keep back neutral and front foot planted.

entries.purpose: Strength and control across a side-to-side squat range
entries.steps: Take a wide stance. Shift weight over one bent leg, sitting toward that hip as the opposite leg straightens to a comfortable degree. Keep foot support secure, return through the center, and alternate or finish one side.
entries.cues: Use a comfortable depth and stable foot contact; the straighter-leg toes can rotate upward naturally if needed.

entries.harder: Progress to light counterbalance or landmine Cossack squat (BFIT-00200).
entries.units: repetitions per side, sets
entries.safety: Not an obligatory deep hip stretch; stay within controllable, symptom-free range.

entries.purpose: Progressive loading and positional strength through a controlled lateral squat
entries.steps: Stand wide holding the end of a securely anchored landmine in front of the torso. Shift over one leg into a controlled lateral squat as the opposite leg lengthens; return to center, then alternate.

entries.easier: Bodyweight Cossack squat (BFIT-00199) or supported lateral lunge (BFIT-00073).
entries.harder: Increase load modestly or expand controllable range, but not both at once.
entries.units: repetitions per side, sets
entries.safety: Verify landmine anchor and clearance; avoid painful pubic/groin positions.

entries.name: Countermovement Vertical Jump
entries.equipment: Clear level landing surface, footwear, sufficient overhead space
entries.readiness: Intermediate; already comfortable landing from small jumps
entries.purpose: Rapid vertical force production after a quick lowering movement
entries.steps: Stand upright, dip quickly through hips and knees to a self-selected shallow-to-moderate depth, then immediately reverse direction and jump vertically. Land under control and reset fully between efforts.
entries.cues: Use one fluid dip-and-drive action; land softly and consistently; keep reps explosive rather than tiring.
entries.mistakes: Exaggerated deep squat; pause at bottom; collapsing or reaching for maximal height without safe overhead space.
entries.easier: Small two-foot jump-and-stick (BFIT-00165).
entries.harder: Add measured jump height or individualized loading once control is stable.
entries.units: jumps/contacts, sets
entries.safety: Different from paused squat jump, which removes the immediate countermovement reversal.

entries.name: A-March
entries.equipment: Clear level outdoor strip or track
entries.purpose: Rehearse upright marching posture, opposite arm-leg timing, and rhythmic foot placement
entries.steps: Travel forward with deliberate alternating steps. Drive one thigh forward to a comfortable height with opposite arm action; place the foot down beneath or close to the hips and repeat.
entries.cues: Stay tall with smooth rhythm; don't lean back to lift the knee.
entries.mistakes: Overstriding; exaggerated knee lift; stiff arms; stomping.
entries.easier: Standing Controlled March (BFIT-00174).
entries.harder: Progress to A-Skip (BFIT-00014).
entries.units: meters, steps, sets
entries.safety: A traveling sprint drill, not an interchangeable alias of standing controlled march.

entries.name: Straight-Leg Sprint Dribbles
entries.equipment: Level clear turf or track; appropriate footwear
entries.readiness: Intermediate; basic upright sprint drill coordination
entries.purpose: Practice compact cyclical foot contacts with tall trunk and limited knee motion
entries.steps: Stand tall and travel forward in very small, rhythmic alternating leg sweeps, keeping knees softly extended rather than locked. Strike lightly beneath the body and increase rhythm gradually without reaching forward.
entries.cues: Feet contact under the body; motion stays small; do not aggressively lock the knees.
entries.mistakes: Reaching far in front, heavy heel striking, over-straightening the knee.
entries.easier: A-March (BFIT-00203) or short controlled marching steps.
entries.harder: Slightly quicker rhythm over a small distance while staying coordinated.
entries.units: meters, sets
entries.safety: Technical warm-up drill, not a maximal speed sprint. Discontinue if calf or hamstring symptoms appear.

entries.name: Flying Sprint
entries.equipment: Suitable level straight lane; approach, timed zone, long safe exit
entries.readiness: Advanced beginner-to-intermediate with prior sprint progression
entries.purpose: Train upright high-speed running after a progressive approach
entries.steps: Use an appropriate progressive approach/run-in to reach fast upright running, maintain a relaxed fast rhythm through a marked flying zone, then continue forward and decelerate gradually over a clear exit. Recover substantially between reps.
entries.cues: Mark approach, flying zone and exit separately; build speed smoothly; measure only the prescribed fly zone.
entries.mistakes: Abrupt deceleration at the fly-zone end; sprinting all-out from the first step; inadequate run-out.
entries.easier: Submaximal progressive build-up (BFIT-00207) or well-spaced strides (BFIT-00186).
entries.harder: Longer flying zone or faster running only with readiness and adequate rest.
entries.units: meters (approach, fly zone, exit), reps, recovery seconds
entries.safety: High-speed hamstring demand. Sprint on clear stable surface and stop if technique degrades.

entries.name: Broad-Radius Curvilinear Sprint
entries.equipment: Clear broad-radius running arc outdoors; safe run-out
entries.purpose: Run quickly while following a predictable broad curve without sharp planned cutting
entries.steps: Mark a gentle, continuous arc. Build speed progressively, follow the arc with coordinated body orientation and foot placement, then run out and slow gradually. Practice both clockwise and counterclockwise when appropriate.
entries.cues: Keep radius broad enough for smooth sprinting; curve running is not a sharp cut or reactive agility.
entries.mistakes: Sudden cuts; tight turns at high speed; leaning beyond control; inadequate exit space.
entries.easier: Larger-radius arc at slower speed, or straight strides.
entries.harder: Moderate speed increase or slightly tighter arc only with good control.
entries.units: meters, repetitions per direction, recovery seconds
entries.safety: At a given effort, tighter curves can limit speed and increase asymmetry; don't call this a pure linear MaxV test.

entries.name: Progressive Sprint Build-Up
entries.equipment: Open level straight area with safe deceleration zone
entries.readiness: Beginner-to-intermediate; adjust final speed to readiness
entries.purpose: Prepare the athlete for faster running through graded, technically controlled efforts
entries.steps: Start at an easy run and progressively increase speed over the designated distance to a planned, submaximal finish, then decelerate smoothly with clear space.
entries.cues: Build rather than jump abruptly to top speed; specify final effort in the workout.
entries.mistakes: All-out sprinting as a warm-up; hard braking; stopping at the marker.
entries.easier: Easy strides BFIT-00186, short distance, lower finishing speed.
entries.harder: Progress final speed or length, not both simultaneously.
entries.units: meters, sets, target relative effort
entries.safety: Do not count the build-up as fly-zone meters unless the workout specifically defines a flying sprint.

entries.name: Half-Kneeling Acceleration Start
entries.equipment: Safe even outdoor ground and clear sprint run-out
entries.purpose: Practice rising from a half-kneeling setup into a short acceleration
entries.steps: Start with one knee on a comfortable surface, opposite foot planted. On a self-chosen cue, rise decisively, orient the body forward, and accelerate for the prescribed short distance.
entries.cues: Keep feet clear of each other on rising; prioritize smooth transition before maximum speed.
entries.mistakes: Jamming rear knee; twisting awkwardly; racing the rise instead of accelerating.
entries.easier: Tall split-stance or standing acceleration (BFIT-00187).
entries.harder: Increase speed once the rise and first steps are controlled.
entries.units: reps, meters, start side
entries.safety: A transition drill rather than a direct substitute for standardized 10m standing-start timing.

entries.name: Sideways Acceleration Start
entries.equipment: Clear outdoor space; stable non-slip surface
entries.purpose: Orient from a sideways posture into forward linear acceleration
entries.steps: Begin side-on relative to the sprint lane. Rotate and reposition the feet to face the intended direction, then accelerate forward for the prescribed short distance, alternating starting side.
entries.cues: Turn safely before driving forward; avoid planting a twisted knee.
entries.mistakes: Hard cut at excessive speed; crossing feet without control; always turning one direction.
entries.easier: Start from a mild diagonal orientation or a forward standing start.
entries.harder: Progress turn speed or varied starting cues once consistent.
entries.units: reps, meters, starting direction
entries.safety: A known orientation transition, not automatically reactive agility.

entries.name: Prone Push-Up Acceleration Start
entries.equipment: Level clean outdoor ground and clear running lane
entries.readiness: Intermediate; ability to move from prone safely
entries.purpose: Practice ground-to-standing transition and short forward acceleration
entries.steps: Begin prone or in a safe low push-up position, hands beneath or slightly outside shoulders. On the cue, press up, bring a foot underneath, stand, and accelerate smoothly over the prescribed distance.
entries.cues: Choose a repeatable starting posture; clear the hands before first sprint steps.
entries.mistakes: Falling forward, rushing the push-up, using a slippery ground surface.
entries.easier: High plank-to-stand transition without sprint, or conventional standing start.
entries.harder: Progress transition speed without sacrificing control.
entries.units: reps, meters
entries.safety: Measure separately from standardized sprint starts; avoid wet, abrasive or unstable surfaces.

entries.name: Supine Acceleration Start
entries.equipment: Level clean outdoor ground; ample space
entries.readiness: Intermediate; can rise quickly without dizziness or imbalance
entries.purpose: Practice rolling or rising from a back-lying position into forward acceleration
entries.steps: Lie on the back in a comfortable repeatable posture. On the cue, roll toward a selected side, plant the hands or feet as needed, rise and face the lane, then accelerate over the prescribed short distance.
entries.cues: Alternate rise direction when appropriate; get oriented before driving; keep the ground transition safe.
entries.mistakes: Whipping the neck; rushing rise before orientation; tripping or running toward obstacles.
entries.easier: Seated-to-stand transition and walkout; standing acceleration.
entries.harder: Progress transition speed and fluency rather than adding distance immediately.
entries.units: reps, meters, preferred roll side
entries.safety: A ground-to-sprint skill, not a pure measure of straight-line acceleration mechanics.

entries.name: Supported Two-Leg Straight-Knee Calf Isometric Hold
entries.equipment: Level nonslip floor and securely fixed rail or counter
entries.purpose: Sustained calf loading and position control with both knees relatively straight
entries.steps: Stand facing a stable support with both feet comfortably apart. Keep knees softly straight, raise both heels to a comfortable height, and hold that height with weight through the balls of both feet. Lower slowly after the prescribed time.
entries.cues: Use hands for balance; keep knees softly straight, ankles steady and weight shared between both feet. Breathe normally.
entries.mistakes: Bouncing; rolling onto the outside of the feet; heels sinking; locking knees or holding the breath.
entries.easier: Use a smaller heel rise or shorter hold and more hand assistance.
entries.harder: Increase resistance or progress to the distinct single-leg hold BFIT-00195 when prepared; change one variable at a time.
entries.units: seconds, sets
entries.safety: Use the guide's dose. Stop for new or increasing pain or loss of position. Persistent tendon pain needs individual assessment; holds do not guarantee injury prevention.

entries.name: Accelerate-to-Stop Deceleration
entries.equipment: Level turf or court; cones; clear run-out
entries.purpose: Control speed reduction over multiple steps
entries.steps: Accelerate over prescribed distance toward marker; progressively brake over several steps and finish balanced before stopping zone. Walk back.
entries.cues: Shorter braking steps, hips and knees bend comfortably, finish stable.
entries.mistakes: Single violent stop; locked knee; slippery surface.
entries.easier: Shorter and slower approach.
entries.harder: Increase entry speed or approach length one at a time.
entries.units: reps, approach meters, recovery
entries.safety: Count braking efforts separately from plyometric contacts. No sharp pain or uncontrolled stops.

entries.name: Planned 45-Degree Cut
entries.equipment: Clear turf/court; approach, plant and 45-degree exit cones
entries.purpose: Brake, redirect and reaccelerate through a predetermined shallow angle
entries.steps: Approach at controlled speed. Brake through preparatory steps before a stable plant, then accelerate along the marked 45-degree exit. Alternate directions.
entries.cues: Prepare to brake before plant, keep balanced foot-knee-hip alignment, accelerate along new line.
entries.mistakes: Late braking; collapsing knee; forced high-speed plant.
entries.easier: Reduce the approach speed or distance; practice accelerate-to-stop deceleration (BFIT-00213) before adding a cut.
entries.harder: Build entry speed while maintaining control; 90-degree cut is distinct.
entries.units: reps per side, approach/exit meters, recovery
entries.safety: Predetermined COD, not reactive agility; grade the speed and angle appropriately.

entries.name: Planned 90-Degree Cut
entries.equipment: Clear flat turf/court; right-angle exit cones
entries.purpose: Practice a sharper direction change with increased braking demand
entries.steps: Approach a marked 90-degree exit at controlled, generally slower speed than a shallow cut. Brake earlier, plant securely and reaccelerate along the perpendicular exit. Repeat both sides.
entries.cues: Brake earlier; keep base stable; turn deliberately before raising speed.
entries.mistakes: Twisting fixed foot; forcing maximal speed; uncontrolled trunk.
entries.easier: Return to 45-degree cut (BFIT-00214).
entries.harder: Increase approach speed only after consistent control.
entries.units: reps per side, approach/exit meters, recovery
entries.safety: Optional in Week 3 only for athletes who demonstrate comfortable control of shallow cuts.

entries.name: Partner Mirror Agility
entries.purpose: Read a leader's real movement and couple decision-making to response
entries.steps: Leader moves unpredictably within a small lane; follower watches leader's hips and trunk and mirrors changes in speed or direction for a brief bout. Switch roles if desired.
entries.cues: Read real motion, maintain safe space, keep bouts short and high-quality.
entries.mistakes: Predetermined sequence; excessive speed; collisions.
entries.easier: Have the leader move more slowly in a narrower lane, use shorter bouts and practice with earlier, easier changes of direction.
entries.harder: More variable speed or late direction changes while staying safe.
entries.units: seconds per effort, efforts, rest
entries.safety: Requires a live mover for opponent-type perception; the solo cue exercise is not equivalent.

entries.name: Partner Two-Gate Chase
entries.equipment: Partner; two gates 3–4m apart; clear noncontact paths
entries.purpose: Respond to opponent's late actual movement choice
entries.steps: A leader starts ahead and makes a late choice of one of two gates. Follower reads leader movement then accelerates or redirects toward the gate without contact. Reset and recover fully between trials.
entries.cues: Respond to observed movement, not predicted routes; control final brake.
entries.mistakes: Guessing early; crossing into collision lane; racing beyond skill.
entries.easier: Partner Mirror Agility (BFIT-00216).
entries.harder: Later gate decision or modest increase in leader speed.
entries.units: chases, gate distance, recovery
entries.safety: Keep paths noncontact and use short controlled chases.

entries.name: Random-Cue Two-Gate Response
entries.equipment: Two cones/gates; independent unpredictable left/right cue audio or helper
entries.purpose: Train response to an unpredictable symbolic direction cue
entries.steps: Stand between two marked gates. Upon an independently randomized LEFT or RIGHT signal, move toward that gate using controlled shuffle or short acceleration, stop and reset.
entries.cues: Cue must be unpredictable; prioritize correct response and controlled stops.
entries.mistakes: Using memorized pattern; calling it opponent-reading; over-speed.
entries.easier: Shorter distance and slower response.
entries.harder: Progress gate distance or cue complexity one variable at a time.
entries.units: efforts, response accuracy, rest
entries.safety: A simpler stimulus-response drill; NOT equivalent to reactive agility involving perception of real opponent actions.

entries.name: Rhythmic Skip
entries.equipment: Clear nonslip turf, court or track; suitable shoes
entries.readiness: Beginner; comfortable marching and small hops
entries.purpose: Develop easy alternating-leg rhythm and coordination before sprinting, cutting or jumping.
entries.steps: Travel forward with small, relaxed alternating skipping hops. Coordinate opposite arm and leg naturally and land softly with short steps; keep knee lift modest and pace easy.
entries.cues: Stay tall and relaxed; rhythm first. Use small, quiet contacts—not a maximal knee drive or forceful projection.
entries.mistakes: Turning it into powerful skipping for height/distance; oversized hops; hard footfalls; rushing while off balance.
entries.easier: March with coordinated opposite arms (BFIT-00203).
entries.harder: Use an A-Skip (BFIT-00014) for more deliberate sprint mechanics, or separately prescribed power skips for height/distance when prepared.
entries.units: metres, passes, low-intensity technique contacts
entries.safety: A low-amplitude coordination drill. Prescribe in short metres or passes. Do not treat as maximal plyometric work; if converted to power skipping, prescribe and count explosive contacts separately.

entries.name: Power Skip for Height
entries.readiness: Intermediate; controls easy skipping and single-leg landings
entries.purpose: Practice alternating explosive upward projection with coordinated arm action
entries.steps: Skip forward using deliberate alternating high takeoffs; drive the opposite knee and arms in rhythm, seek vertical height, land under control, and reset between efforts as prescribed.
entries.cues: Project primarily upward with tall posture; count every explosive takeoff, not every easy walking step.
entries.mistakes: Reaching far forward, forcing knee lift, turning a coordination warm-up into maximal fatigue.
entries.easier: Rhythmic Skip BFIT-00219 or easy A-Skip BFIT-00014.
entries.harder: Raise intent slightly only when elastic landing remains controlled; distance-focused skips are a separate movement.
entries.units: explosive takeoffs, sets
entries.safety: Start with low dose; stop for sharp pain or loss of takeoff/landing control.

entries.name: Power Skip for Distance
entries.readiness: Intermediate; stable lower-body landings and control
entries.purpose: Practice horizontal force projection through repeated alternating skips
entries.steps: Travel forward in alternating powerful skips emphasizing forward projection from each takeoff. Coordinate opposite arms and knee drive, land under control, and reset rhythm before next explosive contact.
entries.cues: Prioritize forward travel without overstriding, excessive braking, or forced reach. Count each explosive takeoff.
entries.mistakes: Collapsing at landing, trying to cover distance solely by reaching the foot, or sprinting instead of skipping.
entries.easier: Rhythmic Skip BFIT-00219; Power Skip for Height BFIT-00220 at easier intent if appropriate.
entries.harder: Increase projected distance modestly or add contacts only if control remains steady.
entries.units: explosive takeoffs, sets
entries.safety: High horizontal loading; keep repetitions short and recover between quality bouts.

entries.name: Forward Gallop
entries.readiness: Beginner; able to march and lightly hop
entries.purpose: Develop asymmetrical forward rhythm and lead-leg coordination
entries.steps: Travel forward with one leg repeatedly leading and the other trailing in a small step-close-hop pattern. Keep contacts low amplitude, then switch which leg leads for the next pass.
entries.cues: Stay relaxed, use small springy motions, and alternate leading legs equally.
entries.mistakes: Repeatedly using only preferred lead; overly forceful bounds; uncontrolled crossing feet.
entries.easier: Step-close marches with no hop.
entries.harder: Increase smooth rhythm slightly, not jump height, before adding load.
entries.units: metres per lead leg, passes
entries.safety: Low-amplitude preparation drill; does not substitute for dedicated maximal bounds.

entries.name: Lateral Gallop
entries.equipment: Flat nonslip court/turf with side clearance
entries.purpose: Develop lateral movement rhythm and alternate leading-leg coordination
entries.steps: Face mostly forward and travel sideways in repeated step-close-hop motions. Keep feet safely spaced and hips controlled. Perform passes with left and right legs leading.
entries.cues: Use soft, low-amplitude contacts and equal left/right leading passes; do not chase speed.
entries.mistakes: Crossing feet unintentionally, bounding maximal distance, turning into a lateral shuffle sprint.
entries.easier: Lateral Step-Touch BFIT-00149.
entries.harder: Slightly quicker rhythm while retaining relaxed low-power contacts.
entries.units: metres per lead leg, passes
entries.safety: A coordination gallop, not a high-intensity lateral bound.

entries.name: One-Foot Penultimate Walk-through
entries.equipment: Clear flat lane with footfall markers if useful
entries.purpose: Rehearse comfortable final approach steps preparing ONE-foot takeoff, without forcing a jump
entries.steps: Start from a short 3–5-step approach at walking/jogging speed. Rehearse the penultimate-to-final transition that sets up a ONE-foot takeoff, finish balanced without jumping, and return to reset. Alternate intended takeoff legs.
entries.cues: Let approach speed and body position guide step length; do not artificially reach far ahead or lean backward.
entries.mistakes: Exaggerated long penultimate, hard braking, confusing a two-foot gather with unilateral takeoff.
entries.easier: Slow walking rehearsal with fewer steps or marked foot placements.
entries.harder: Progress rhythm at a modest jog; add a separate one-foot short-approach jump BFIT-00226 only when ready.
entries.units: rehearsals per takeoff leg
entries.safety: Technical rehearsal only; no explosive landing counted unless a jump is added.

entries.name: Two-Foot Penultimate Walk-through
entries.readiness: Beginner-intermediate; comfortable foot placement and balance
entries.purpose: Rehearse final steps leading to a coordinated two-foot plant, without requiring a jump
entries.steps: Use a short 2–4-step approach at a controlled walk or jog. Rehearse a comfortable penultimate-to-final step and two-foot plant with feet at a manageable width, finishing balanced and upright enough to jump without doing so.
entries.cues: Find a repeatable gather rhythm; avoid a fixed universally prescribed long penultimate.
entries.mistakes: Heel jamming, crossing feet, overlong step, uncontrolled hip/trunk rotation.
entries.easier: Walking two-foot gather with deliberate pauses.
entries.harder: Progress to a short approach with a controlled two-foot jump BFIT-00227.
entries.units: rehearsals, sets
entries.safety: Controlled approach rehearsal, not a maximum vertical jump or universal jump style.

entries.name: One-Foot Short-Approach Jump
entries.equipment: Clear safe run-up and soft/stable landing zone; optional reachable target
entries.readiness: Intermediate; comfortable single-leg landing and walk-through approaches
entries.purpose: Convert controlled horizontal approach into a one-foot jumping takeoff
entries.steps: Take 3–5 comfortable approach steps, organize the last two steps for a ONE-foot takeoff, jump upward or slightly forward as prescribed, and land safely with enough clear space. Practice both takeoff legs when appropriate.
entries.cues: Build rhythm rather than maximum approach speed; use measured start mark; count one contact per deliberate jumping takeoff.
entries.mistakes: Overlong penultimate, reaching, landing in obstructed space, maximizing speed before technique.
entries.easier: One-Foot Penultimate Walk-through BFIT-00224; small single-leg hop-and-stick BFIT-00228.
entries.harder: Slightly faster controlled approach or increased takeoff intent, not both at once.
entries.units: jumps per takeoff leg, sets
entries.safety: Never use a hard unsafe landing from maximal height; adapt target and surface to readiness.

entries.name: Two-Foot Short-Approach Jump
entries.equipment: Clear short approach lane and safe landing area
entries.readiness: Intermediate; controlled two-foot plants and landings
entries.purpose: Convert a short approach into a coordinated two-foot takeoff
entries.steps: Take 2–4 comfortable approach steps, gather into a stable two-foot plant, jump vertically or as specified, then land under control with ample clearance. Reset between attempts.
entries.cues: Maintain repeatable approach and plant rhythm, with gradual projection into the takeoff; count one jump event per attempt.
entries.mistakes: Exaggerated penultimate reach; uncontrolled feet crossing; repeated landings with poor alignment.
entries.easier: Two-Foot Penultimate Walk-through BFIT-00225; CMJ BFIT-00201.
entries.harder: Increase approach speed modestly with good plant and landing consistency.
entries.units: jumps, sets
entries.safety: Do not use an elevated basket/rim or object if the landing area is unsafe.

entries.name: Single-Leg Hop-and-Stick
entries.equipment: Level stable non-slip floor with space
entries.readiness: Beginner-intermediate; controlled single-leg stand and low hop
entries.purpose: Train small one-leg propulsion and balance control after landing
entries.steps: Balance on one leg, make a small controlled upward or forward hop from that leg, land on the same leg, and hold balance about two seconds before resetting. Repeat prescribed contacts on both sides.
entries.cues: Small, quiet landing, trunk over supporting foot; reset rather than rebound rapidly.
entries.mistakes: Large uncontrolled leap, rapid continuous pogo contacts, knee buckling, forcing unstable end range.
entries.easier: Single-leg stand or supported step-to-stick; Small Two-Foot Jump-and-Stick BFIT-00165.
entries.harder: Gradually increase hop distance or height before considering reactive hops; keep hold consistent.
entries.units: landings per leg, sets
entries.safety: Low-amplitude landing drill rather than depth jump. Stop for sharp discomfort or poor landing control.
